data.one_liner: Render server-driven UI layouts designed in the Codelessly Editor natively in Flutter.
data.what_it_does: Allows you to design screens in the Codelessly Editor, publish them, and render them natively in your app with live updates, data binding, actions, and navigation. Supports loading by public slug, Firebase project token for live updates, or offline via asset bundles.
use_when: You want to update your app's UI dynamically without shipping a new app release.
You want to build or prototype screens using a visual editor or an agent-driven compact notation.
avoid_when: You need fully offline-first local UI architecture without external remote configuration or bundles.
You rely completely on Linux desktop and need live Firebase updates (Firebase is not supported on Linux).
strengths: Enables live updates of screens without app store releases.
Multiple loading modes including slug, live Firebase token, or local offline asset bundles.
Integrates smoothly into Flutter render objects with custom function hooks and data binding.
weaknesses: Firebase-backed live updates do not support Linux desktop.
Relies on external Codelessly Editor infrastructure for authoring screens.
data.setup_notes: Simply add the dependency and optionally initialize with a slug, token, or local asset bundle.
data.minimal_example:
final codelessly = Codelessly(config: const CodelesslyConfig(slug: 'my-project'));

runApp(MaterialApp(home: CodelesslyWidget(codelessly: codelessly)));
